name: CTX photo layer for the MarsWay EVA area
dataset: Murray Lab Global CTX Mosaic of Mars, beta01 (uncontrolled), ~5 m/px
credit: NASA/JPL/MSSS/The Murray Lab (Caltech); tiles hosted by Esri
license: Murray Lab grants free use of beta01 for all purposes (Esri service description)
reference: Dickson et al. (2023), Global CTX Mosaic of Mars, https://murray-lab.caltech.edu/CTX/
source_crs: Mars 2000 sphere (R 3396190 m), geographic / plate carree
project_crs: Mars 2000 sphere, Equidistant Cylindrical, centre lon 0 (metres)

coverage.mask: Source alpha and black empty-service pixels; bilinear sampling uses premultiplied alpha to avoid dark gap borders.
coverage.note: Transparent pixels expose the terrain basemap; coverage is not a registration accuracy claim.

limitations: beta01 is an uncontrolled mosaic. Registration to the USGS DEM has not been established; offsets of tens of metres or more are possible. Matching crop bounds do not establish pixel-level alignment.
Esri serves lossy 8-bit JPEG tiles; brightness is not calibrated reflectance.
CTX is 5 m/px: it shows ridges, hollows and dunes, not individual rocks. HiRISE is needed for boulders.

alignment_check.reason: Exploratory brightness/shading correlation is not independent image registration. No shift applied; best-search offsets are diagnostic only.
alignment_check.method: FFT cross-correlation of band-passed CTX brightness vs DEM shading (Sun azimuth searched in 30 degree steps), 5 m grid, search +-100 m
alignment_check.note: Exploratory best-search offsets are not measured image offsets or an accuracy bound. No correction was applied to ctx.png.
